questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: They offered courses that were not offered at my home university and had a good reputation regarding research and teaching on sustainability, critical theory, climate, and environment

questions.answer: The only option in Lund is off-campus housing. It was a bit difficult, but there are a lot of options and places to look

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The only option in Lund is off-campus housing

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It's a long time ago i registered for courses so I don't remember the process very well anymore. But I remember that it was quite elaborate and a bit confusing. And the receiving institution made a mistake and signed me up for other courses that I had registered for.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You received an elaborate guide on how to register that was helpful

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses that I registered for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Expect that it takes time and that there are a lot of steps and application material you have to provide

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the level of the courses suitable for a master programme. I was challenged in some ways, but did not feel lost or incapable of following the courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style of the courses I took were very different. But in general there were more lectures and more student-led seminars where the students were more involved in shaping the course.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Human Ecology: Culture, Economy and Ecology
Gender Global Development, and Postcolonialism

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend both of the courses I took, especially the course on human ecology

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I did not participate in activities specifically for students. I participated in volunteer work and sports clubs that were dis-connected from the university and open for everyone

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend getting engaged in the ecosocialist collective and volunteering at People's Kitchen and the Alnarp Fram

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go for hikes in the nature surrounding Lund

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: As a Danish person it was quite easy to adjust to the Swedish culture

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I found it difficult to socialise with local student, but a tip is to live at a student dorm with many local students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any challenging cultural differences

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I don't know

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Lund is a small and quiet town, which I found perfect for me, but for other people it might be a bit too small and calm.

- Be prepared for a big work load, but good quality teaching

- The Swedish people can be difficult to get to know

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new and inspiring people with whome I had a lot of values and interests in common

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The semester is divided in two parts, so you change courses in the middle of the semester. It was hard having to start over and meet and get to know a lot of new people on the new courses

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
